	python -m coverage report --show-missing --skip-empty --skip-covered

clean:
	rm -rf build/
	rm -rf dist/
	rm -rf ./*.egg-info

build:
	python -m build --sdist --wheel

release: clean build
	python -m twine upload -u __token__ dist/*

mkdocs-local:
	mkdocs serve

mkdocs-push:
	mkdocs gh-deploy --force

# Generate Insta-Load snippet and update it in the docs
regenerate-insta-load:
	python wat/inspection/insta/regenerate.py wat/inspection/inspection.py README.md docs/index.md wat/inspection/insta/instaload.py

example-inspect:
	python docs/example/example_inspection.py

mkdocs-index:
	python docs/mkdocs_gen.py generate-index

build_recipe.rationale: The successful setup trajectory required three sequential package installations: (1) pip install -e . installs the wat package in editable mode making the wat module importable; (2) pip install pytest pydantic installs the test framework and required modeling library; (3) pip install nuclear installs the nuclear sublog dependency required by tests/asserts.py. The first pytest attempt (without PYTHONPATH) failed with ModuleNotFoundError for 'tests' module because the tests package is not a subpackage of wat. The second pytest attempt (with PYTHONPATH=/app) failed with ModuleNotFoundError for 'nuclear' because nuclear was not yet installed. The final successful verification required PYTHONPATH=/app to locate the tests package at the repository root level. All three pip install commands are preserved as separate build_commands to maintain the exact installation order that enabled successful test collection. The PYTHONPATH setting is placed in runtime_preparation_commands since it must be set before test execution but is not a build-time mutation.
